liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Lazy Lightnin'** (1 review): Bob's transition from Lazy Lightning into Supplication is highlighted as a gem [24]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The performance of The Other One is specifically called a gem by the reviewer [24]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): The reviewer remembers the jam at the end of Scarlet Begonias into Fire vividly [26]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance had missed changes, though the Saint peak was great [34]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-04-23.143127.fob.senn421.wise.clugston.miller.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 25 songs; 182 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1983-04-23.143126.fob.senn421.wise.clugston.miller.flac1648**: audience recording; 25 songs; 182 min [2]
- **gd1983-04-23.163834.senn441.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 188 min [6]
- **gd1983-04-23.fob.senn421.jeffm.1864.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 22 songs; 187 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [11]. Said about its sound: The tape needs EQing but is considered better than board recordings generally [34]
- **gd1983-04-23.117598.Sennheiser421.daweez.d5scott.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 173 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [17]. Said about its sound: This source is described as very full sounding and well EQed compared to others [31]

## Around the show

- Phil was turned up from the start, and everyone was hot that night [23]
- The New Haven Coliseum venue was imploded two years after this concert [25]
- Attendee arrived on acid, ate a cigarette in the car, and found the scene wild [26]
- The reviewer expressed anger about the venue's demise and the resulting scene changes [28]
- Attendee went dressed as a clown with friends from New Canaan, CT [33]
- Dave Lindsay gave the clown-dressed attendee a ride home after losing the costume [33]
- Considered one of the most highly underrated shows of the 1983 tour [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-04-23.143127.fob.senn421.wise.clugston.miller.flac2496**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Wise's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell UDXLII C90) [1]. Also: Two sets of masters were used to create this complete recording [1]
- **gd1983-04-23.143126.fob.senn421.wise.clugston.miller.flac1648**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Jim Wise; source: Jim Wise's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell UDXLII C90) [2]. Also: Two sets of masters were used to make this recording complete [2]
- **gd1983-04-23.163834.senn441.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics (16th row, DFC) > Sony D5M [6]. Also: Rob Eaton provided the recording, transfer, and harddrive for this source; Jim Wise's Sennheiser 421 source supplies a patch in Drums and the encores [6]
- **gd1983-04-23.fob.senn421.jeffm.1864.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jeff M.; source: FOB-Sennheiser 421>Master Cass(Sony D5)>Dat [11]
- **gd1983-04-23.117598.Sennheiser421.daweez.d5scott.flac16**: taped by Da Weez; transferred by D5scott; source: Source: 2 Sennheiser 421 microphones > Sony TC-D5M - analog master cassettes; [17]
